# Scenario shocks

## Overview
`ems_scenario_shock()` is an intertemporal shock type that specifies heterogeneous shocks at the tuple level as absolute values.
By default, inputs must cover all pre-aggregation tuples and span the full extent of the variable; with `partial = TRUE` they may cover only some of the aggregated tuples (see [Partial scenario shocks](#partial-scenario-shocks)).
Values must be in the same units as the underlying database coefficient; at deployment they are summed over the set mappings of [`ems_data()`](data_load.qmd), and each year's aggregated value becomes the percentage change from the base-year value (the ordinary change for a variable declared `(change)`), so the same input serves any aggregation.

```r
ems_scenario_shock(
  var,
  input,
  partial = FALSE
)
```

| Argument | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `var` | Character | Variable name as it appears in the model file |
| `input` | Data frame or Character | Data frame or path to a CSV file containing all pre-aggregation tuples, a `Year` column (chronological years), and a `Value` column (absolute values) |
| `partial` | Logical | If `TRUE`, `input` may cover only some aggregated tuples; only those are shocked (default `FALSE`) |

## Using scenario shocks
Scenario shocks differ from custom shocks in a number of respects:

1. Only available for intertemporal models

2. Inputs must contain all *preaggregation* tuples associated with a variable, unless `partial = TRUE`

3. Inputs are denominated in absolute values in the units of the underlying database coefficient (e.g., million $USD, population)

4. The input data frame or CSV must contain a `Year` column of chronological years, the base year included, since each later year's shock is the change from the base-year value

There are several applications where it is advantageous to use scenario shock rather than a custom shock.
The primary advantage is that scenario shocks allow for seamless changes to model aggregations since the shocks themselves are subject to mappings and aggregation.
If we have trajectories available for all tuples within a given variable, a scenario shock will adjust to set mapping inputs in `ems_data()`.
Because values are summed over the pre-aggregation tuples before the percentage change is taken, they must be levels in common real units (e.g., persons, million USD).
Index values such as a base of 1 for every country would give an aggregated region the unweighted mean of its members' growth rather than their size-weighted growth; they are safe only when no tuple is aggregated.

## Population trajectory example
Here is an example that takes base year population data from the GTAP database (typically not read into the model) and constructs hypothetical pathways for every region in the model.
These pathways are valid for any regional aggregation chosen.

Set up the model run with chronological time steps:
```r
year <- 2017
time_steps <- year + c(0, 1, 2, 3)

dat <- ems_data(
  dat_input = "v7_data/gsdfdat.har",
  par_input = "v7_data/gsdfpar.har",
  set_input = "v7_data/gsdfset.har",
  time_steps = time_steps,
  REG = "big3",
  ACTS = "macro_sector",
  ENDW = "labor_agg"
)

GTAP_RE <- ems_example("GTAP-RE", tempdir())
model <- ems_model(
  model_file = GTAP_RE[["model_file"]],
  closure_file = GTAP_RE[["closure_file"]]
)
```

Load POP at full regional resolution (unaggregated) as the scenario baseline.
The `REG = "full"` call does not require `time_steps` since it is only used to extract the base-year coefficient:
```r
pop <- ems_data(
  dat_input = "v7_data/gsdfdat.har",
  par_input = "v7_data/gsdfpar.har",
  set_input = "v7_data/gsdfset.har",
  REG = "full",
  ACTS = "macro_sector",
  ENDW = "labor_agg"
)$POP
```

Construct trajectories with compound growth through each future time step.
`tail(time_steps, -1)` yields the forward time steps, keeping the trajectory in sync with whatever `time_steps` was passed to `ems_data()`:
```r
pop$Year <- year
regions <- unique(pop$REG)

pop_traj <- expand.grid(REG = regions, Year = tail(time_steps, -1),
                        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
pop_traj$Value <- 0
pop <- rbind(pop, pop_traj)

set.seed(42)
growth_rates <- data.frame(
  REG = regions,
  growth_rate = runif(length(regions), min = -0.01, max = 0.05)
)

pop <- merge(pop, growth_rates, by = "REG")
base_values <- pop[pop$Year == year, c("REG", "Value")]
names(base_values)[2] <- "base_value"
pop <- merge(pop, base_values, by = "REG")

pop$Value[pop$Year > year] <-
  pop$base_value[pop$Year > year] *
    (1 + pop$growth_rate[pop$Year > year])^(pop$Year[pop$Year > year] - year)

pop$growth_rate <- NULL
pop$base_value <- NULL
pop <- pop[order(pop$REG, pop$Year), c("REG", "Year", "Value")]
```

`ems_data()` returns coefficients with plain set names (e.g., `REG`).
Rename to the model's set-index convention before passing to `ems_scenario_shock()`:
```r
colnames(pop)[colnames(pop) == "REG"] <- "REGr"
```

Pass `pop` as the scenario shock and deploy:
```r
pop_trajectory <- ems_scenario_shock(
  var = "pop",
  input = pop
)

cmf_path <- ems_deploy(
  .data = dat,
  model = model,
  shock = pop_trajectory
)
```

`pop` may also be saved as a CSV and loaded directly by passing the file path to `input`.

## Partial scenario shocks {#partial-scenario-shocks}
Sometimes trajectories exist for only part of a variable, for example the population of a single region.
With `partial = TRUE`, a scenario shock covers only the aggregated tuples its input fully supplies.
Every pre-aggregation tuple that maps to a shocked aggregated tuple must be present, in every year.
An aggregated tuple that is only partly covered stops the deployment by name, because the percentage change of a partial sum is not the change of the whole group.

Continuing the example above, the following shocks population in the United States and China only, which are their own regions in the `"big3"` aggregation:
```r
pop_partial <- pop[pop$REGr %in% c("usa", "chn"), ]

cmf_path <- ems_deploy(
  .data = dat,
  model = model,
  shock = ems_scenario_shock(var = "pop", input = pop_partial, partial = TRUE)
)
```

The shocked tuples must be exogenous, and exogenous tuples outside the input keep a zero change.
The same input stops under an aggregation that groups the United States with other countries, unless those countries are supplied as well.
Since values are summed over the pre-aggregation tuples, scenario shocks, partial or not, suit additive variables such as values and quantities.
